Hi all — quick technical notes from my side. Long version below, TL;DR at top.

TL;DR:
- Yes — reranker can emit structured JSON per candidate ("category","confidence","annotations"). Use the streaming structured-output flag in the SDK and set response_format="json_per_candidate". No code change to model, SDK param only.
- Determinism: floating-point vs quantized variants can reorder ties; recommend deterministic-seed tests and compare NDCG/precision deltas across model variants.
- Auth/routing checklist: SAML SSO for console, API keys for programmatic with IP allowlist. For dedicated PoC, request a temporary dedicated pool (no extra entitlements), but ensure VPC peering if they require private network.

Detailed notes:
1) Structured output/tool-calling: Our reranker supports structured outputs via the SDK param response_format and supports tool-calling hooks for downstream facet extraction. The JSON schema we return per candidate: {"candidate_id":string,"score":float,"predicted_category":string,"confidence":float,"explain_tokens": [string]}. For the PoC use response_format=\"json_per_candidate\" and set max_tokens small since this is metadata-only.

2) Top_k semantics and tuning: The ranking API takes candidates + features and returns a ranked list. top_k parameter controls how many are returned, but metric behavior differs: precision@1/precision@3 and recall@10 are your primary knobs. For tuning: start with top_k=20 to collect recall signals and then evaluate precision@1 and NDCG@5 to pick the operational top_k (likely 3–5 for UI). Also run slice analysis on short queries separately.

3) Quantization/determinism: Quantized kernels can introduce slight score perturbations. For determinism: run seeded runs with the same model variant, enable deterministic kernels (dev flag), and run pairwise rank-stability tests (Kendall tau) between baseline float and quantized. If Kendall tau < 0.85 on critical slices, escalate to model team for calibration.

4) Embedding + reranker compatibility: If they plan hybrid scoring (embedding similarity + reranker score), normalize embeddings to unit length and specify a consistent scoring weight. We support passing precomputed embeddings as candidate features (embedding vector serialized as base64). Recommend 1536-d embeddings for compatibility unless ClearSearch uses a different vector size — mention that in the PoC so we can map dims.

5) Evaluation metrics and tooling: baseline set: precision@1, NDCG@5, recall@10, MAP. We can run Redwood's eval harness and output a slice CSV; recommend two slices: short queries (<=3 tokens) and long-tail (<= 1 request frequency). We'll provide an eval script (python) that hits our local SDK and emits metrics.

6) Operational: for the PoC, use hosted API with IP allowlist + API key; if they want dedicated, we can provision a temporary reserved pool for 2 weeks. Canary plan: run 10% traffic through reranker + 90% baseline, monitor precision@1 delta and latency p95.

I'll attach a sample auth matrix and small eval harness later today. Happy to jump on a tech workshop if you want to walk through the SDK calls.

—Karthik
